Compute the pressure distribution inside a centrifuge spinning at 10,000 RPM using the rotating-fluid equilibrium equation dP/dr = ρ·r·ω², not the static hydrostatic formula P = ρgh.
Convert 10,000 RPM to angular velocity: ω = 10,000 × 2π/60 ≈ 1047.2 rad/s.
Integrate the equilibrium equation from a reference radius outward to obtain P(r) = P(r₀) + ρ·ω²·(r² − r₀²)/2.
Use water as the default working fluid with density ρ = 1000 kg/m³, and treat density as an input parameter so the calculation works for any fluid.
Use gauge pressure with the reference condition P(r₀) = 0.
Set the reference radius r₀ = 0 (the axis of rotation), so the distribution simplifies to P(r) = ρ·ω²·r²/2.
Compute the distribution over the radial range r = 0 to r_max = 0.1 m (10 cm), and treat the outer radius as an input parameter.
Report the pressure at radial sample points r = 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, and 10 cm, and present the distribution as a continuous curve from r₀ to r_max.
State all assumptions (fluid density, reference radius, reference pressure, radial range) explicitly in the output.
Optionally, show the pressure distribution for two or three different fluid densities (e.g., water 1000 kg/m³, blood plasma 1025 kg/m³) to illustrate the dependence on ρ.
